sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Public Registry of Panama national corporate jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (code-based system with hybrid Anglo-American corporate law influences, including the Private Interest Foundation regime)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States of America Bilateral Investment Treaty (1982)
Panama–Republic of Korea Double Taxation Treaty (2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT regime, as reinforced by Law 70 of 2019); Executive Decree No. 95 of 2020; Resolution UAF No. 059-2017 (Sistema de Registro de Titulares de Beneficiarios); Law 2 of 2010 amending Law 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); Resolution of the Dirección General del Registro Público No. 165-2013 (PIF inscription and registered agent obligations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of the passport of the foundation founder and each council member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority of the country of issuance (Civil Registry or official passport-issuing ministry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled bank reference letter (creditworthiness and professional standing) for the founder and council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank duly regulated in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized foundation charter (escritura pública constitutiva) and organization council acceptance letter

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under Article 42 of Law 23 of 2015; mandatory screening of the founder, council members, beneficiaries, and protector (if any) against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU CFSP sanctions list, and the domestic list maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); documented risk rating and UBO determination must be retained in the foundation's internal compliance file for at least five years after the termination of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Plataforma de Registro en Línea del Registro Público de Panamá (online name availability certification portal of the Public Registry of Panama)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory naming conventions require use of the Spanish alphabet script; foreign names and extended-character words must be transliterated into the local script; the corporate denomination must contain or be followed by the word 'FUNDACIÓN' (Foundation) or an accepted equivalent evidencing foundation status; abbreviations, punctuation, and numerals are subject to the normalization rules of the Registro Público de Panamá.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, the applicant or the resident agent shall file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá within ten business days of notification, stating the legal grounds and including the certified name search code; the Registry must resolve within the statutory administrative period, and the denied party may subsequently pursue a contentious-administrative appeal before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally not accepted as the sole registered office for a Panama Private Interest Foundation with commercial operations; the foundation must be represented by a licensed resident agent with a physical Panamanian address; external business centre addresses may be accepted only when the resident agent maintains the required physical presence and the operating entity secures separate municipal commercial address for the specialty tea salon.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the foundation shell holding stage (estimated 8% likelihood of unannounced inspection per fiscal year), but medium (estimated 35%) for the operating specialty tea salon because municipal sanitary and commerce inspections under Panama's environmental and food-service rules are routine.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and name availability certificate (Certificación de Denominación Social) from the Registro Público de Panamá
Preparation and notarization of the foundation charter (escritura pública) before a Panamanian notary
Hague Apostille certification on the foundation charter and supporting personal documents through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular and apostille statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Private Interest Foundation inscription and inscription fee at the Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration tariff based on declared foundation capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent (registered agent) formation retainer and provision of statutorily mandated registered office services in Panama for one year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent law firm in Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial establishment of the internal UBO file, PEP screening, OFAC/UN sanctions check, and AML risk assessment (Expediente de Debida Diligencia) for the foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foundation's resident agent / AML compliance officer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal notice of operation (Aviso de Operación) and commercial license application for the specialty tea salon in the Municipality of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alcaldía Municipal del Distrito de Panamá

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUC (Régimen Único de Contribuyente) application and pre-incorporation tax-clearance processing at the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official administrative processing fees and legal filing benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of June 12, 1995, as amended, on Private Interest Foundations, regulated by Executive Decree No. 1003 of December 13, 1996. Applicable sections: Articles 1-8 (formation and charter contents), Articles 9-14 (organization of the Foundation Council), and Articles 20-24 (beneficiaries and foundation rules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry), Dirección General, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundations Section), Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación de Fundación de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundation Charter), executed as a notarized private instrument before a Panamanian notary and registered with the Public Registry in certified copy.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required under Law No. 25 of 1995; the Foundation must have an identifiable initial patrimony or endowment contributed by the Founder (market practice: at least USD 10,000). Panama does not mandate a paid-up capital escrow, deposit certificate, or bank verification at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL - The Founder and the initial Foundation Council, acting under Law No. 25 of June 12, 1995, as amended, hereby RESOLVE: (a) the initial endowment contributed by the Founder is accepted and recorded in the Foundation's patrimony; (b) the registered office is fixed at the Resident Agent's office, [AGENT], Panama City, Republic of Panama; (c) [PERSON] is appointed President, [PERSON] Secretary, and [PERSON] Treasurer of the Foundation Council; and (d) the officers are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and implement the Foundation's purpose, including the operation of a specialty tea salon lounge. APPROVED unanimously on [DATE], at [PLACE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Licensed Resident Agent and Draft Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm acting as Resident Agent; Notaría Pública del Circuito, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a locally licensed attorney as Resident Agent. Instruct preparation of the Foundation Charter in Spanish, specifying the founder, foundation name, registered office at the agent's address, initial endowment, purposes, beneficiaries, Foundation Council composition, and any reserved rights of the Founder. Execute the charter before a Panamanian notary after legal review.
required_dossiers: Passport or valid ID of the Founder
Proof of address of the Founder (utility bill or bank reference)
Details of beneficiaries and protector, if any
Indication of initial endowment and source of funds
Notarized power of attorney if the Founder is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Resident Agent flags deficiencies, amend and re-execute the charter before filing; no government penalty applies at this pre-filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize the Foundation Charter and Obtain Certified Copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito (Circuit Notary Public), Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder or attorney-in-fact appears before the notary to sign the Foundation Charter. The notary authenticates signatures and issues certified first and second copies (copias certificadas) required by the Public Registry, plus two sealed plain copies.
required_dossiers: Signed Foundation Charter
Original documents proving the Founder's identity or legal capacity
Written notarial instructions
Receipt of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial authentication is refused due to irregular signatures, obtain fresh signature legalization, apostille, or consular certification of foreign documents before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified copy of the notarized charter, two sealed copies, and the official registration request through the online Sistema de Intermediación Digital (SID) or the Public Registry's citizen service windows. Pay the official registration fee of approximately USD 300 by treasury deposit or bank cashier's check. The Registry examines the legality of the charter and issues the inscription (registro) granting legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Foundation Charter
Two sealed copies of the charter
Public Registry registration request form (solicitud de inscripción)
Proof of payment of official registration fee
Written acceptance of appointment by the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or objection (defecto), file a written remedial response (subsanación) within 30 calendar days addressing each observation; registry staff normally grant one corrective turn to perfect the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification Number (RUC) and Municipal Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipality of Panama - Tesorería Municipal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Foundation's RUC at the DGI, or through the SID online portal, attaching the Registry inscription and Resident Agent's data. Register the economic activity under ISIC 5630 / NAICS 722515 for the specialty tea salon lounge if the Foundation operates the business directly. Subsequently present the RUC and the sanitary permit application to obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación (business license) and zoning certificate at the Municipality of Panama.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription certificate of the Foundation
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Accreditation of the Resident Agent
Foundation Council appointment minutes
DGI RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente)
Municipal business license form with activity description, floor plan, and zoning certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is returned, correct taxpayer category or legal representation errors and re-file; municipal license objections are cured by submitting the MINSA sanitary permit and a valid zoning certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Foundation Rules, Hold First Council Session, and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (Consejo de la Fundación) and Resident Agent; regulated banking entity in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Private Foundation Rules (Reglamento) detailing Council administration, quorum, voting, and beneficiary rights. Convene the first Council meeting to adopt the First Board Resolution, approve internal governance, and authorize banking instructions. Submit the resolution and KYC/AML documentation to a regulated Panamanian bank to open the operating account for the tea salon lounge.
required_dossiers: Executed Foundation Rules (Reglamento)
First Board Resolution (pro-forma as approved)
Certified IDs and bank references of appointed officers
Bank account application and KYC forms with source-of-funds evidence
Registry inscription, RUC, and municipal license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional due diligence, provide audited source-of-wealth documentation or a Resident Agent's comfort letter; if the Council is defective, the Founder may exercise reserved rights to amend the Charter or Rules by supplementary notarial instrument.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección General de Salud, Departamento de Protección de Alimentos; Municipality of Panama - Tesorería Municipal
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento for Food and Beverage Establishments (sanitary operating permit) and Municipal Aviso de Operación / Patente Comercial

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I - Registration (Declaración de Impacto Ambiental) applicable to small food-service establishments; a low-risk specialty tea salon operating in an existing commercial building may qualify for an exemption certificate under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 of August 14, 2009, subject to MiAMBIENTE screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0233-2002 for discharges to municipal sewer - pH 6-9; BOD5 no greater than 200 mg/L; TSS no greater than 220 mg/L; oils and greases no greater than 50 mg/L; no untreated food residue or tea sediment. Air emissions: compliance with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 15 of August 2, 2006 on air quality for kitchen ventilation and extraction systems, including volatile organic compound and particulate limits for stationary sources. Solid waste: mandatory segregation and disposal under Law No. 51 of 2020 (Circular Economy Law) with a municipal waste collection contract.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: SINAPROC (Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil) fire-safety technical inspection and certification covering extinguishers, emergency exits, alarms, and signage; Municipality of Panama structural and occupancy clearance for the commercial unit; MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral) workplace risk assessment and occupational hygiene compliance; CSS (Caja de Seguro Social) employer registration for all staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); electronic filing and registration portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa); e-invoicing authorizations issued pursuant to DGI Resolution No. 201-5360 and subsequent amendments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) already inscribed in the Registro Público must obtain a taxpayer registration number (RUC, Registro Único de Contribuyente) prior to commencing business operations. Procedure: (1) appoint a resident legal agent/abogado and register the foundation's economic-beneficial-owner declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) with the DGI; (2) file the RUC application online via the Sede Electrónica using Form RUC-15, attaching the foundation charter (Escritura Pública), padrón certificate, local business lease, and board resolution authorizing the tea salon activity; (3) select the applicable tax regime: standard corporate ISR (25%) or the Pequeño Contribuyente simplified regime if expected annual gross income is between B/.36,000 and B/.200,000; (4) register for ITBMS liability and, if staff are hired, as an employer with DGI-Secretaría CSS; (5) obtain the municipal aviso de operación (business license) and integrate the DGI e-invoicing system by requesting an authorized facturador electrónico or the DGI Web-Invoice module, plus an X.509 digital signature for invoice clearance. Ordinary turnaround is 5–10 business days after presentation of the municipal license.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope / Entity_Level_Taxation. The PIF is a distinct taxable person under Art. 692 of the Código Fiscal: only Panamanian-situs income is subject to corporate ISR at 25% (or the 5%–15% progressive small-taxpayer scale if the applicable gross-receipts election is made). Foreign-source foundation assets and offshore income remain outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction. The PIF is not eligible for pass-through treatment in Panama; the local tea salon turnover is attributed to and taxed at the foundation level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Régimen de Pequeños Contribuyentes (Law 66 of 2016 and Art. 714-A of the Fiscal Code): election for taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding B/.200,000, replacing ordinary ISR with a simplified fixed quarterly contribution measured on gross receipts (2% on commercial sales) while ITBMS continues at 7%; (2) standard regime election with full ITBMS input-credit deduction where annual gross income exceeds B/.200,000; (3) cash-basis accounting election under Decree 170 of 1993 for qualifying small businesses; (4) depreciation and exempt-zone elections under Law 41 of 2007 for investments in less-developed provinces; (5) no 'check-the-box' equivalent exists; territorial sourcing applies mandatorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios — Panamanian VAT/GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No universal financial exemption threshold—any person performing taxable acts on Panamanian territory (including rental of salon premises, sale of prepared tea beverages, and retail ceramic goods) must register for ITBMS. Small-taxpayer simplification available up to B/.36,000 annual gross income; mandatory e-invoicing phase-in thresholds: taxpayers with annual gross income ≥ B/.500,000 were required to issue electronic invoices from 2021, and all registered taxpayers (including small merchants) must be fully integrated into the DGI electronic invoicing framework with fiscal ticketeras or facturador electrónico modules as of December 2023.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama imposes mandatory near-real-time electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance. The PIF must transmit XML-formatted invoices (schema v2.0, DGI annexes) to the DGI through an authorized facturador electrónico using a bidirectional HTTPS API and an X.509 digital signature. The DGI validates each invoice, assigns a unique 'expediente de comprobante' number (digital stamping), and returns a validation code; B2C point-of-sale transactions are transmitted in daily batches using an approved fiscal ticketera, with night-time synchronization. Failed schema validation, duplicate invoices, or missing QR codes trigger automatic rejection and per-invoice penalties (from USD 100 to USD 500 under DGI Resolution No. 201-3605 as amended). All export and zero-rated transactions must still be electronically reported with fiscal code 'E', including the associated DUI number.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to (a) physical exports of loose-leaf tea, tea wares, and specialty ceramic products sold to non-resident consignees provided the goods physically depart Panamanian customs territory within 180 days of the sale and are covered by an accepted DUI export declaration; and (b) services wholly rendered and economically consumed outside Panama (e.g., digital tea-culture instruction or offshore consulting activities of the foundation). Domestic in-salon prepared tea, take-away beverages, and local retail sales to residents and tourists remain subject to 7% ITBMS and may not be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUI (Declaración Única de Aduanas) export declaration duly accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas with exit stamp and proper HS tariff lines (HS 0902 for tea; HS 6912 for ceramic ware)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill indicating the foundation as shipper and a non-resident consignee, with port of discharge and precise cargo description matching the DUI
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 issued by the receiving Panamanian bank evidencing transfer of the export proceeds from the foreign buyer, and
Commercial invoice and packing list cross-referenced to the DUI, plus (if available) the international freight contract and marine insurance certificate proving cross-border movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI runs biannual cross-matching audits comparing DUI export records, freight manifests, shipping-line databases, and bank inflows. Zero-rating claims that are unsupported by physical exit or international remittance within the 180-day window are per se reclassified as local taxable sales: ITBMS is assessed at 7% retroactively, plus 25% ISR understatement interest accrue at 1.5% monthly (Art. 1054, Código Fiscal). Civil penalties range from 100% to 200% of the net tax or refund claimed (Art. 741, Código Fiscal); criminal liability attaches under Art. 346-A of the Código Penal where false declaratory documents exceed USD 10,000, carrying imprisonment of 4 to 8 years and mandatory cancellation of the export registration for three consecutive fiscal years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). Panama does not maintain a central bank; the U.S. dollar serves as legal tender alongside the Panamanian balboa at a fixed 1:1 parity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system with no central bank issuing discretionary domestic currency and no statutory exchange controls. Both capital account and current account transactions are freely convertible, with no general restrictions on profit remittances, dividends, or capital repatriation for domestic and foreign investors. The balboa exists only as a unit of account and as coinage; all banking liabilities are U.S. dollar-denominated. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to standard corporate governance formalities and withholding tax obligations under the Territorial Taxation regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation requiring the surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion of export receipts in Panama. Exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds in any offshore or domestic account, and all receipts are freely negotiable in the U.S. dollar financial system. Mandatory conversion ratios are not applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Panama permits digital banks and electronic payment institutions under the SBP licensing framework on a sandbox or full-branch basis, but pure offshore digital EMIs without a local physical office have limited viability. Foreign fintechs generally require incorporation, licensing, and a representative office in Panama. Existing special fintech banking licenses allow multi-service electronic money issuance, yet compliance burdens and capital requirements remain material. A fully regulated, physically present Panamanian bank account is strongly preferable for establishing liquidity rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated for the initial face-to-face verification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of a Private Interest Foundation. While Panama has adopted electronic onboarding tools and video-call KYC for low-risk clients, banks commonly require at least one director or an appointed agent to appear in person at the bank's premises. Remote opening is possible only for clearly documented low-risk corporate structures with a pre-existing banking relationship or an SBP-approved digital onboarding module; otherwise, in-person interview is a practical precondition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer shares or incomplete UBO declaration in the Private Interest Foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incumbency, Foundation Charter with full UBO schedule, apostilled passport copies, reference letters from a licensed Panamanian attorney and a corresponding bank, plus a sworn affidavit identifying every beneficiary and confirming compliance with Law 23 of 2015 and FATF recommendations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth inconsistency or junior-level initial funding from non-transparent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the founder, signed wealth declaration with bank statements from the remitting account, bank reference from an existing institution, tax residence certificates, contracts or invoices evidencing the commercial origin of funds, and legal entity ownership chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political Exposed Person (PEP) status of the foundation protector or beneficiary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed PEP declaration, explanation of legitimate source of funds, fit-and-proper letters from reputable counsel, enhanced due diligence questionnaire, copies of the underlying wealth-generating instrument, and an independent third-party legal opinion on the legitimacy of the PEP engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transaction profile mismatched with specialty tea lounge operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with projected sales volumes, supply contracts with tea producers, customs and import documentation for ceramic products, landlord lease agreement, local operating licenses (Aviso de Operación and Municipality permit), and evidence of proposed POS and credit card processing arrangements in Panama.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be executed via SWIFT MT103 or equivalent U.S. dollar wire to the PIF's Panamanian bank account. Panama does not impose exchange controls; however, the remitter should clearly state the purpose code corresponding to 'Financial Assistance / Capital Contribution' or 'Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Investment' for banks' AML profiling. The Panamanian receiving bank may require a copy of the foundation resolution, UBO information, and source-of-funds documentation. Funds are cleared in Fedwire or via correspondent U.S. banking network with normal one to two business day settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for specialty tea importation and cultural ceramic purchases are processed using SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) for deferred or documentary trade finance. Panamanian banks provide U.S. dollar-cleared disbursements through their correspondent global network. Where the counterparty is in a non-dollar jurisdiction, the disbursement leg may involve a correspondent conversion into local currency at prevailing market rates. Trade payments should be linked to commercial invoices, packing lists, and shipping documents to satisfy SBP anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market tea-origin currencies such as CNY, INR, VND and IDR
Cross-currency swaps for tenor-matched funding in EUR, CHF, or RMB
OTC options on USD/EUR and other G10 crosses, executed via a licensed international counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) — mandatory annual fee to maintain the PIF's legal existence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), with payment recorded at the Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 30 each year; collection window runs from January 1 through June 30 without extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% surcharge (B/.15) from July 1; 10% (B/.30) from October 1; after December 31 monthly interest of 1.25% accrues, all registry filings and certificates are blocked, and sustained unpaid delinquency (10 consecutive years) triggers administrative strike-off by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de Beneficiarios Finales) — UBO annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales de Personas Jurídicas (centralized beneficial ownership registry under Law No. 254 of 2020)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the filing window set by DGI resolution (first statutory deadline: July 31, 2022; subsequent annual windows published each year, generally in the first half of the year); change of beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines per Executive Decree 130 of 2021 (up to B/.10,000); outstanding UBO declaration blocks the issuance of the paz y salvo (good-standing certificate) and registration of any foundation act; false UBO data carries criminal exposure under Panama's AML/tax crime legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operating License Annual Renewal (Aviso de Operación / Patente Municipal) for the specialty tea salon lounge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio de Panamá (or the municipal authority of the district where the salon operates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 31 of each calendar year (annual renewal for the new fiscal period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal surcharge of 10% per year or fraction of the unpaid rate plus interest; failure to renew for two consecutive years triggers revocation of the operating patent, closure orders, and asset attachment by the municipal enforcement office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta ISR — Form 105/105-F) for Panama-source income generated by the tea salon operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 15 of the year immediately following the calendar tax year (or the next business day where March 15 falls on a weekend or public holiday)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax due per month (capped at 100% of the tax) plus 1.25% monthly interest and late-payment surcharge; repeated non-filing may escalate to criminal tax charges under Panama's tax crime statute (Law 76 of 2019) and enforced collection through bank attachments.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or investment incentive applies to ISIC 5630 specialty tea salon operations in Panama. The territorial tax regime excludes foreign-source income from the taxable base. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) operating a tea salon may elect the Small Taxpayer Simplified Regime under Law 91 of 2019 if annual gross income does not exceed B/. 200,000, resulting in an effective tax of 2% on gross receipts instead of 25% on net taxable income. This elective regime is the only materially relevant rate-reducing mechanism for this business activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario DGI-1020 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed through Panama's e-Tax 2.0 portal at https://etax.dgi.gob.pa, using the RUC of the PIF and the resident agent's credentials.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return and tax payment are due no later than 15 March of the following calendar year. For a PIF using a different fiscal year end, the return is due within three months after the end of that fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC and full legal name of the Private Interest Foundation; domicilio fiscal of the resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners must not use their foreign identity numbers in this box. Enter the Panamanian RUC of the PIF and, if acting through a resident agent, the agent's RUC and notarised address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered by the declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the calendar year unless the DGI has previously granted an alternative fiscal year. Non-resident foundations cannot create a custom tax year without formal DGI approval.

Enter CIIU code 5630 for the specialty tea salon lounge operation. A PIF whose commercial activity is purely conducted by a separate Panama operating entity should select the applicable ISIC code of that entity and indicate 'through direct operations' in the clarification field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña: gross receipts from tea and ceramic product sales, salon service fees, and cultural event ticketing sourced in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF has no Panama-sourced income because all tea salon sales are executed in a foreign branch, enter zero and attach an affidavit explaining the territorial exclusion. Under no circumstances should foreign-source revenues be disclosed as Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deducciones autorizadas: allowable expenses attributable to Panama-source gross income, including inventory procurement, rent, wages, utilities, licenses, depreciation, and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-administered PIF, deduct only costs directly connected to Panama-source operations. Parent company overhead, travel expenses to Panama, and costs of foreign management are not deductible against Panama-source income without a tax-pository support showing economic benefit to the Panama operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta neta gravable, impuesto causado, anticipos, and final tax payable or tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% on net taxable income or 2% on gross receipts if the small taxpayer regime has been elected. Subtract deferred tax credits and quarterly prepayments. If the result is a loss, enter zero for the tax due and reflect the loss carryforward for use in Box 6a of subsequent years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and payment trigger a monthly surcharge of approximately 2% of the assessed tax due, with a statutory floor of B/. 100 and a ceiling of 50% of the tax owed. The DGI additionally applies default interest on unpaid tax at the official monthly rate, suspends electronic invoice authorisation for repeated non-filing, and may impose administrative fines of up to B/. 10,000 for material non-compliance with formal filing requirements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividend distributions paid by a Panamanian PIF from profits that have borne the 25% corporate income tax. If the distributed profits originated from untaxed or exempt Panama-source earnings, the applicable withholding rate is 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding rate under a Panama double tax treaty, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate from the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction for the relevant calendar year; (2) legalise or apostille the certificate, translate it into Spanish by a qualified residing translator, and present it to the paying PIF at least five business days before the dividend distribution; (3) execute a beneficial ownership statement confirming that it is the undisputed economic recipient of the dividend; (4) file a separate treaty relief request with the DGI using the electronic portal and annex the TRC; and (5) retain a stamped copy in the foundation's minutes and tax records. If the DGI denies the relief, the payer must withhold the full statutory rate, and the foreign owner may pursue an administrative refund within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for trademarks, patents, copyrights, or industrial know-how used in Panama are Panama-source income and are subject to a statutory 25% withholding tax; DTA relief commonly reduces this rate to between 5% and 10%. Interest payments made by a PIF to an unrelated foreign financial institution on an arm's-length loan are generally not taxed in Panama because the interest is considered foreign-source income. Interest paid to related non-bank foreign lenders in respect of funding used in a Panama tea salon operation is subject to a statutory 6% withholding tax, with treaty rates typically ranging from 0% to 5%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama's transfer pricing rules require taxpayers with consolidated Panamanian-source gross revenue exceeding B/. 3,000,000 in the prior fiscal year to prepare and maintain Local File and Master File documentation and file Form 1050-TP. In addition, aggregate related-party transactions exceeding B/. 1,500,000 trigger a materiality-based disclosure obligation. A specialty tea salon below these thresholds is not automatically required to file the TP report, but must retain a contemporaneous memorandum explaining any cross-border tea leaf procurement and management service pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not yet apply a codified Economic Substance Regulation mirroring the UAE or Bermuda regimes; however, the DGI applies a substance-based anti-abuse principle under the territorial tax system and general anti-avoidance provisions. A PIF operating a specialty tea salon lounge must prove economic substance through a lease or ownership of the salon premises, licensed food-service staff, utility bills in the foundation's name, comprehensive business insurance, and daily electronic sales records. Lack of physical presence, pitch-dark decision-making outside Panama, and absent payroll or inventory evidence will cause the DGI to disregard the foundation and recharacterise its income as belonging to the foreign beneficial owner, with interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of cash tea sales from the POS system, understatement of beer is not applicable to tea salon but understatement of gross receipts using a second manual cash book, false purchase invoices from uncontracted related tea suppliers, payroll under-reporting of wait staff, or destruction of daily e-invoice summaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's Código Fiscal Article 761-A and the Criminal Code, the entity is liable for a fine equal to two to five times the evaded tax, plus monthly default interest, suspension of the food-service license, and, upon conviction, imprisonment of two to five years for the natural persons responsible. The DGI may also impose an administrative penalty of 100% of the tax amount omitted from the return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the resident agent, and the treasurer who sign a false or fraudulent return are personally and solidarily liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax and penalties. Criminal prosecution attaches to the individuals, not the PIF, and includes attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced upon proof of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Foundation Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a pure form vehicle with no physical tea salon, no leased commercial space, no permanent employees, no inventory records, and no actual business transactions while maintaining foreign bank accounts and investments under the foundation's name to mislead regulators about the true owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama Law 42 of 2020 and registry jurisprudence, a foundation found to be a sham may be dissolved for lack of lawful purpose or false representation. The DGI may assess tax on the worldwide income of the foundation's beneficial owner if management and control are in fact exercised from Panama, and impose administrative fines up to B/. 50,000 for failing to comply with substance notification requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered resident agent are personally liable for knowingly facilitating a sham foundation. Civil orders may be issued requiring restitution of dividends, the resident agent may be suspended from practice, and foreign non-resident directors may face extradition or, if asset tracing reveals fraud within Panama, personal seizure and denial of re-entry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting structured cash payments of B/. 10,000 or more in tea salon transactions without customer due diligence, using simultaneous POS and manual cash records to launder unknown-cash flows, transferring funds to sanctioned foreign related companies without reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit, or allowing the PIF's bank account to be used for unexplained third-party clearing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama Law 23 of 2015 imposes fines on legal entities from B/. 10,000 to B/. 1,000,000 per violation, mandatory license suspension of the food service establishment, freezing of bank accounts, and criminal sanctions of imprisonment for five to twelve years for money laundering under the Criminal Code. Named reporting officers also face monetary fines and permanent disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated compliance officer are personally liable if they knowingly fail to perform KYC, fail to report suspicious transactions, or approve transfers from an unexplained cash pool. The law enables asset seizure, travel interference to prevent departure, and extradition agreements with foreign jurisdictions for laundering proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Intra-Group Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sourcing premium loose-leaf tea through a related Hong Kong or Swiss intermediary at a mark-up exceeding the open-market CUP by 40%, paying 'cultural branding' fees to an affiliated jurisdiction with no actual service rendered in Panama, or setting a royalty for tea name usage at a non-commercial level to transfer profit from the Panama operation to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI will recharacterise the related-party transactions under the arm's-length principle, increase taxable income by the overstated expense, impose the additional 25% corporate tax on the adjustment, apply monthly interest, and add a penalty equal to 25% of the tax deficiency. Intentional manipulation may additionally expose the entity to tax evasion criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the inflated procurement or management service contracts are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency, interest, and penalties. Under fiduciary duty principles, the foundation may file a civil claim against them; DGI can issue distraint orders against their personal bank accounts, impose travel bans during the assessment, and report them to criminal authorities for knowing participation in the false pricing.
